strategies.comments:
Other Options

Wormadam-G has Rock Blast for stronger damage against Flying-types like Emolga, Pelipper, and Mothim, but Wormdam-G loses to most of these foes, can still wear them down with Toxic, and is better off focusing on its positive matchups. Although Earth Power OHKOes Lairon, Earthquake still threatens Lairon while doing more damage to foes such as Muk, Arbok, and Mienfoo. Skill Swap has niche use to disrupt Clefairy's Magic Guard, but Wormadam-G is hard-pressed to fit such a specific move despite Clefairy otherwise walling it.

Checks and Counters

Clefairy: Clefairy walls Wormadam-G thanks to Magic Guard ignoring passive damage, and it can use it as an opportunity to support its teammates with its utility moves, leaving Wormadam-G to only set up Stealth Rock and potentially lose its Leftovers to Knock Off.

Staryu: Staryu can remove Wormadam-G's Stealth Rock and threatens to 2HKO with Scald. Staryu can remain healthy against Wormadam-G thanks to Recover and Natural Cure.

Taunt: Stealth Rock and Toxic define Wormadam-G's role, and Persian, Mienfoo, and Bibarel can prevent it from using them. Frillish and Vullaby can wall Wormadam-G if it cannot use Toxic on them.

Grass-types: Meganium and Leafeon can take advantage of Wormadam-G's passivity to set up and break through it or support their teams, and both have moves to alleviate or avoid Toxic. Ivysaur and Gloom wall Wormadam-G thanks to their Toxic immunity.

Ground-immune Pokemon: Toxic is often Wormadam-G's only good move against anything immune to Ground. Emolga and Pelipper both carry strong moves against Wormadam-G and can come in freely before Stealth Rock is up. Solrock can use Wormadam-G as an opportunity to set Stealth Rock, and though defensive sets can't beat Wormadam-G on their own, Wormadam-G is more threatened by Will-O-Wisp than Solrock is by Toxic.

Strong Super Effective Special Attacks: Glaceon threatens to OHKO Wormadam-G, and though Walrein dislikes Toxic, it can 2HKO Wormadam-G. Raichu and Simisear fear Earthquake, but Simisear OHKOes Wormadam-G and Raichu can OHKO it with Hidden Power Ice after a Nasty Plot.

Residual Damage: Poison and burn negate Wormadam-G's passive recovery and make it worse as a wall. Muk can fish for a poison on Wormadam-G while it switches in, and opposing utility Pokemon like Wormadam-S, Hippopotas, and Vibrava commonly carry Toxic.

movesets.name: Utility
movesets.description:
Thanks to its unique typing and physical bulk, Wormadam-G can reliably set up Stealth Rock as it checks common physical attackers like Mienfoo, Muk, and Arbok. Although Wormadam-G is not very strong uninvested, many physical attackers, such as Lairon, Muk, and Pawniard, are Ground-weak, so they are often 2HKOed by its Earthquake. Wormadam-G's Earthquake is also strong enough to break Substitute on foes hit neutrally by it, such as Walrein, Kingler, and Whiscash. Protect maximizes Leftovers recovery for Wormadam-G, and it has additional perks like allowing Wormadam-G to block Persian's Fake Out and scout Choice item attackers like Glaceon and Mr. Mime. Toxic has great synergy with both Earthquake and Protect, and it lets Wormadam-G put a timer on opposing walls like Frillish and Hippopotas and Ground-immune foes like Solrock and Pelipper. Alternatively, Wormdam-G can run Bug Bite to break Leafeon's Substitute, but it's quite weak against foes it's not super effective against. Sucker Punch lets Wormdam-G pick off weakened foes like Grumpig, Mr. Mime, and Persian, though, like Bug Bite, it's not very strong. Anticipation is not that useful, but it's the best ability Wormadam-G has, and it can be useful to scout for super effective coverage moves on Muk and Arbok.

Bulky offense teams appreciate the role compression Wormadam-G provides by setting Stealth Rock and blanket checking several physical attackers, and its teammates can compensate for its limited damage output without needing it to be a pure wall. Muk and Mienfoo make excellent partners for Wormadam-G; they appreciate it checking Poison-types for them while they threaten Clefairy for it. Walrein can check Clefairy and Glaceon for Wormadam-G, and it capitalizes on Wormadam-G's Stealth Rock when it forces switches. Grass-type partners like Leafeon are great for Wormadam-G, as they threaten Water-types like Staryu and Frillish, and they benefit from it checking Poison-types for them and setting up Stealth Rock to wear down the Flying-, Fire-, and Ice-types that threaten them. Meganium can remove status from Wormadam-G with Aromatherapy and capitalizes on Wormadam-G's Stealth Rock with Dragon Tail.

strategies.overview: The only thing Wormadam-G has going for it in NU is its unique typing, which allows Wormadam-G to function as a unique wall. However, its movepool is bare outside of Stealth Rock, it's slow, and it has no reliable recovery moves, making it easy bait for most setup sweepers. Most of the time, you are better off using defensive Piloswine, or Golurk.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Rest is a viable option because status cripples Wormadam-G and it appreciates the recovery, but Wormadam-G doesn't learn Sleep Talk, so a cleric partner such as Audino or Lickilicky is necessary if Wormadam-G takes that route. Psych Up can be used with Wormadam-G so it can take on Pokemon such as Bulk Up Gurdurr and Calm Mind Musharna better. However, Wormadam-G still cannot do much damage to those Pokemon, so it is generally not worth it. Wormadam-G has access to weather moves, but it is outclassed by Pokemon with better abilities, offenses, and typings. Bug Bite is an optional second STAB, and Rock Blast can be used to hit the Flying-types that counter the set. Bulldoze or Rock Tomb can be used to slow down switch-ins. Lastly, Wormadam-G has access to Swagger, but its reliability is too luck based to perform well.

Checks and Counters

Any super effective Flying-, Fire-, Ice-, or Water-type coverage move checks Wormadam-G since it has no reliable way to heal itself; RestTalk users and Guts users of those types outright counter Wormadam-G. Grass-types resist Earthquake and have many ways to minimize or neutralize Toxic damage, such as Tangela with Regenerator, LumRest Exeggutor, and Substitute Serperior. Taunt users also shut down Wormadam-G, especially Mandibuzz, Misdreavus, and Serperior, all of which take little to no damage from Earthquake. Substitute users such as Braviary and Sawsbuck, which are immune to and resist Earthquake, respectively, can avoid Toxic and can set up on Wormadam-G. Poison-types that are not weak to Earthquake, such as Roselia and Weezing, can easily attack or set up on Wormadam-G. Lastly, clerics can eliminate all of the status that Wormadam-G spreads.

movesets.name: Utility
movesets.description:
Stealth Rock is the most important move in Wormadam-G's arsenal because it deals constant, reliable damage to the opposing team. Other than that, all Wormadam-G can really do is stall with Toxic and Protect. Protect also scouts for super effective attacks and racks up Leftovers recovery, which can be useful at times. Earthquake is Wormadam-G's most reliable attacking option, as it hits the Poison- and Steel-types that are immune to Toxic super effectively.

To benefit its stalling, Wormadam-G really appreciates Toxic Spikes support from Pokemon such as Roselia and Garbodor. Fire-types such as Charizard and Torkoal also make good partners for Wormadam-G since they cover its weaknesses and can take out Grass-types that can manipulate this set. Water-types such as Carracosta and Samurott cover many of Wormadam-G's weaknesses and also make good partners.
